articles.title: Mark Ruffalo Tells Rob Bonta ‘Don’t You Dare’ Settle the Antitrust Lawsuit Against Paramount: ‘Do Not Cave’
articles.summary: Mark Ruffalo is encouraging California attorney general Rob Bonta and his coalition of 11 other state AGs not to settle their lawsuit against Paramount Skydance and keep David Ellison from acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery. “Don’t you dare, [Rob Bonta], do not cave,” Ruffalo wrote on X.
body: Paramount Skydance’s $111 billion deal for Warner Bros. was approved by the Department of Justice in June. However, the deal was put on hold thanks to the antitrust lawsuit from Bonta and his team of state AGs. The Wall Street Journal, citing anonymous sources, reported Friday that Paramount Skydance and Bonta are in “advanced talks” to reach a settlement.

Ruffalo isn’t the only one asking Bonta to hold his ground. Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts wrote on Facebook Saturday morning that President Donald Trump banning CNN from the White House is a warning of things to come if Paramount Skydance swallows Warner Bros. (Trump also banned MSNOW and Politico).

“As Trump tries to ban CNN from the White House, it would be a massive mistake to cave on the Paramount merger,” Warren wrote. “The last thing we need is another Trump-controlled media conglomerate abusing its power to stomp out competition. This is a dangerous merger.”

articles.title: ‘Ride or Die’ Canceled by Prime Video After One Season
articles.summary: “Ride or Die” has been canceled by Prime Video after one season, Variety can confirm. The streamer’s Hannah Waddingham and Octavia Spencer-led buddy dramedy premiered in July of this year. It was first reported that Spencer and Waddingham were teaming up for the series in December 2023.
body: In her review of Season 1, Variety ’s Aramide Tinubu wrote that “‘Ride or Die’ works best when it fully leans into the ‘Thelma & Louise’ aspects of the central storyline… Spencer and Waddingham have a robust and genuine chemistry — a companionship that will undoubtedly resonate with countless viewers. Moreover, watching Waddingham as a full-fledged action star is something everyone should be witnessing on a daily basis.”
Other cast members included Ed Skrein, Calam Lynch, Savannah Steyn, Jamie Parker, and Jacky Ido, with Sylvia Hoeks and Bill Nighy.

Tessa Coates created the series and serves as executive producer and showrunner along with Matt Miller and director Peyton Reed. The show is produced by Paramount Television Studios, Amazon MGM Studios as well as Andy and Barbara Muschietti’s Double Dream and Octavia Spencer ’s Orit Entertainment. Coates, Miller, and Reed executive produce alongside Spencer for Orit Entertainment; Waddingham; Andy Muschietti, Barbara Muschietti, and Irene Yeung for Double Dream; Brian Clisham; and Stephanie Kluft.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran Addresses Macklemore Controversy While on Stage at First Concert Since Rapper Dropped From Tour: ‘What Is Happening in Gaza Is Catastrophic and Unjustifiable’
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran addressed the controversy surrounding Macklemore’s removal from his Loop Tour on Saturday night, speaking from the stage at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field during his first concert since the rapper was dropped from the trek.
body: Saturday’s concert marked Sheeran’s first performance since a tumultuous week for the U.S. leg of his Loop Tour, which saw Macklemore removed from the remaining dates following the rapper’s onstage remarks in support of Palestinians during Sheeran’s Sept. 4 and 5 shows at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

During his MetLife performances, Macklemore spoke about the war in Gaza and the West Bank and told the stadium crowd, “Free Palestine.” His set also included “Hind’s Hall,” his 2024 protest song supporting Palestinians. The remarks drew criticism from some Jewish and pro-Israel organizations, including the Israeli-American Council, which called for Macklemore to be removed from the tour.

Messina Touring Group, the promoter behind the U.S. leg of the Loop Tour, subsequently announced that Macklemore would no longer appear on the remaining dates. The company said venues had informed the promoter that they would not allow concerts featuring Macklemore to proceed, a situation it said could have resulted in cancellations affecting hundreds of thousands of ticket holders.

articles.title: Ruby Rose Remembers ‘Best Friend’ Hayden Panettiere: ‘All That She Ever Wanted Was to Have Her Story Told’
articles.summary: Ruby Rose got emotional when asked about her friend, Hayden Panettiere, who died Aug. 16 at 36. Rose told Entertainment Tonight that Panettiere was her “best friend” and that they “spoke every day for five years.” “I didn’t even think we were going to be friends,” Rose said, tearing up.
body: The two quickly became close after realizing they “had everything in common,” Rose said. Throughout their five-year friendship, they texted each other every day to check in.
“Hayden, all that she ever wanted was to have her story told her way, on her terms,” Rose said.

Panettiere, who was known for her roles on “Heroes,” “Nashville,” “Scream 4” and “Scream VI,” openly spoke about her struggles with drug and alcohol addiction in her 2026 memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning.” Days after her death, the Drug Enforcement Administration joined the investigation, working with South Carolina’s Greenville Police Department to determine her cause of death.
Hollywood stars shared tributes online after news of her death became public, including Jack Coleman, who played her father on “Heroes.”

articles.title: Matthew Rhys' sister 'so proud of him' after historic Emmy wins
articles.summary: Rhys, from Cardiff, became the first person to win two lead acting Emmy prizes in one night.
body: The sister of Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys said her family had been "pinching ourselves all week" following his historic Emmy success.

His older sister Rachel Evans, who accompanied Rhys to the ceremony in Los Angeles, said she was starstruck seeing Hollywood royalty at the event, and revealed that she and her brother called their parents afterwards, who were sat at home in their dressing gowns.
Speaking to Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales, Evans said watching Rhys win the awards was "an experience I will never ever forget or probably match".
She said that as the "bossy" older sister, she told him that morning that he needed to prepare, adding: "If you win, you cannot wing it."

body: Ed Sheeran addressed the ongoing controversy surrounding the removal of Macklemore from his Loop Tour during Saturday’s stop in Philadelphia at Lincoln Financial Stadium.

Sheeran continued, “I don’t want to disappoint fans, and I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet. My concerts have always been a safe space for everyone, and that matters hugely to me. Honoring my commitment to my fans is also completely essential to who I am, and that is why I’m here tonight on my own and continuing my current tour.”

The “Thinking Out Loud” singer said he was “deeply worried about the idea that venues pre-approve content for performance.” He added, “This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world.”
Sheeran continued, “Now, I want to address the question of where I stand in the situation in Israel and Palestine.”

articles.title: Amanda Redman: ‘My most embarrassing moment? Getting caught doing a pretend Bafta thank you speech’
articles.summary: The actor on a terrible accident as a toddler, her bossy nature, and feeling too old to play a Shakespearean heroine. Born in Brighton, Amanda Redman, 69, studied at Bristol Old Vic theatre school. She starred in the TV comedy drama El C.I.D.
body: When were you happiest? I am happiest when I have my daughter and granddaughter with me.

What is your earliest memory? Being in hospital. I was standing up in a cot and we were being asked what we wanted for lunch. I think it was Great Ormond Street. I had managed to pull a cauldron of boiling turkey and vegetable soup all over me when I was 18 months old, and I spent five years of my life in various hospitals.
Which living person do you most admire and why? Barack Obama, for his decency. I felt real hope when he was elected, which has been dashed now.
What is the trait you most deplore in others? Meanness of spirit.

articles.title: ‘He’s simply astonishing’: will Andrew Scott become the first out gay man to win the best actor Oscar?
articles.summary: The Irishman seems a dead cert for his performance as Ian Charleson in Elsinore. And his ability to avoid being pigeonholed while embracing queer stories, from Pride to All of Us Strangers, is a remarkable achievement.
body: This Sunday, the curtain falls on the Toronto film festival, the last of the three big autumn showcases – alongside Venice and Telluride – that are launchpads for award campaigns. And as the dust settles on the red carpets, one name rises above the others as destined for sure-fire glory: Andrew Scott.

The Irish actor, 50 next month, is now not only considered a lock for a leading actor Oscar nomination but almost certain to take the prize next spring. Should he win, he will become the first out gay actor to do so in the Academy’s almost 100-year history.

If that’s a fact that seems astonishing today, it would have felt an inevitability in 1989, when the film for which Scott has been so praised is set. In Elsinore, he plays Ian Charleson, the dashing Scottish star of films including Chariots of Fire and Gandhi. Charleson had been given his first role three years before Chariots by Derek Jarman, but excised it from his CV (leading to a lifelong rift, depicted in Elsinore). Muting his sexuality was then considered essential in the pursuit of stardom. Yet despite such curation – and his undeniable talents – Charleson never reached the level of fame he felt he deserved.

articles.title: Naomi Watts Dedicates Donostia Award to Her ‘Mulholland Drive’ Director David Lynch: “I Miss You”
articles.summary: At the San Sebastian Film Festival Saturday night, Watts also shouted out her 'The Impossible' co-star Tom Holland and explained why she was grateful to be getting opportunities "as a woman of my age."
body: British star Naomi Watts dedicated her Donostia Award to the late, great David Lynch on Saturday night.

Watts picked up San Sebastián Film Festival’s most prestigious honor before a screening of her latest feature, The Housewife. She was introduced by J.A. Bayona, the Spanish filmmaker who directed Watts in 2012’s The Impossible, which would earn the actress her second Oscar nomination.

Watts was emotional as she came to collect the award and thanked Bayona for his kind words. “Shooting in Spain with incredible crews, getting to know the Thai community, so many full, brilliant memories, and I loved it all, the whole experience, even the hard stuff,” she said about The Impossible, which grossed over $198 million at the global box office upon its release. “Even doing 30 takes in the water tank, submerged,” she laughed, shouting out her co-star Tom Holland, who made his live-action debut in the film aged 15. “Tom Holland called it the best water park he ever went to. I called it pure pain!”

articles.title: From ovations in Venice to death threats in Israel: the extreme responses to NAZA documentary
articles.summary: As Gaza documentary wins cinematic acclaim, its directors face vitriol in Israel amid a febrile election campaign. First there was a moment of stunned silence. Then, in the Sala Grande, the main screening hall of the Venice film festival within the Palazzo del Cinema, the audience stood almost as…
body: The film the audience had watched for 80 harrowing minutes was the Gaza documentary NAZA, which has been produced by the Guardian.
The film’s title comes from an Israeli military acronym used euphemistically to refer to the civilians expected to be killed in a military attack.

Unfolding against the background of Tel Aviv at night, the participants – intelligence officers and other soldiers – describe a series of systems, some powered by AI, that select the thousands who should die in strikes, often at night and surrounded by their families.
Perhaps most challenging for Israel’s political elite is that it is a story told exclusively in Hebrew by 24 anonymised Israeli military insiders, many of them from elite units.

articles.title: Is SNL New Tonight? (September 19, 2026)
articles.summary: Is Saturday Night Live new tonight? Here's everything to know about the next SNL host, musical guest, air time, and what's coming next in Season 52.
body: The late night television staple "Saturday Night Live" is heading into Season 52, continuing to deliver live sketch comedy following its milestone 50th anniversary celebration not too long ago. While the cast and writing staff continues to change, showcasing today's rising stars in comedy, Lorne Michaels remains the show's fearless leader, even as rumors perpetually swirl about his potential retirement.

As we head into the fall and shows return to network television, you're probably wondering whether "SNL" is new on this evening of September 19, 2026. Thankfully, we've got all the details you need to know about the return of "SNL" for Season 52, as well as the upcoming episodes that have already been announced.

No, there is not a new episode of "Saturday Night Live" on September 19, 2026. This is the last weekend of the annual summer hiatus that network television shows often take, giving their cast and crew a break for a few months before getting back to work.
Thankfully, you won't have to wait to long for a new episode of "SNL," because Season 52 is about to begin before the end of September.
